did: I built Android Compat, a workflow you start by hand to stamp a release's Android compatibility on slowed emulators. For each API level it runs the launch test, then a pull storm against a stand-in home with sample data, and writes a table, a release-note line and JSON. Its first runs showed the pull storm on 34 and 36 before HERD1, and a blank page on old images whose WebView is below 111. I added the page that tells such a phone to update WebView from Play (#3123). The emulator then showed the page never appeared, because the app's own start replaced it, so I fixed that and proved it on API 24 and 31 through every way in (#3141). Once HERD1 and HERD2 landed, the storm check turned out to judge the app by rules HERD never promised; with HERD's owner I rewrote it to their own rules (#3139). The rewritten check then caught a real lane drop after a trip home, and the second run its first fix caused; HERD fixed both in HERD4 (#3148), and with it the stamp is green on 34 and 36.

calls.title: How the stamp slows an emulator
options: one core, 1.5 GB, a 3G link and a 60% CPU cap
a larger runner with a real slow-device profile
calls.why: The older S21 Ultra showed the storm and the S26 hid it; a slowed emulator stands in for the slower phone on GitHub's free runners.
calls.undo: Change the emulator options and cpu_percent's default in android-compat.yml (C543).

calls.title: How the stamp pairs with a stand-in home
options: https with a CA made per run, put in the emulator's system store
a user CA or a network config change in the app
calls.why: The app's manifest and network config stay exactly as shipped, so the stamp tests the real release.
calls.undo: Drop trust-ca.sh and pair unpaired; a level without the CA already says "no system CA" (C544).

calls.title: Which build the storm runs on
options: the release APK, paired through its own Pair form
the debug APK, driven over DevTools
calls.why: The stamp should say what the shipped app does; a level that can't drive the form falls back to the debug build and its row says so.
calls.undo: Run storm.sh's pair_by_page path for every level (C545, which moved C542).

calls.title: Which commit the stamp builds
options: the branch or tag it is run from, with no ref input
any ref typed into an input
calls.why: Building another ref from main's run is the cache poisoning CodeQL flags; the coordinator accepted this for you.
calls.undo: Add a ref input back to android-compat.yml (C547, which moved C541).

calls.title: What a phone with a WebView too old for the app shows
options: Capacitor's own check loading a static page with Play buttons for WebView and Chrome
a script in index.html that swaps the page
calls.why: Capacitor already compares the WebView's version; a static page with no script shows on any WebView.
calls.undo: Unset android.minWebViewVersion and server.errorPath in capacitor.config.ts (C548).

calls.title: How the stamp treats an old level below WebView 111
options: test that the update page shows through every entry, and fail on a blank page
skip it and never read red
calls.why: The blank page went unseen because those levels were skipped; testing them found the defect #3141 fixed.
calls.undo: Restore run-level.sh's skip below MIN_WEBVIEW (C549, which moved C546).

left: #3146: once, on API 34, the launch test's drag at the jobs wing never checked again; it didn't recur, and it needs a few more 34 runs to tell the emulator from PULL5.
#3140, the pull's "unread" line while a joined run is still reading, is HERD's story, not this session's.
The throwaway branch claude/compat-herd4-proof (a proof run, nothing to keep) needs deleting by hand: the git proxy refuses branch deletes from sessions.
The joined phase can't see a dropped lane that makes only one read; noted on #3139, not fixed.
An optional certificate date window for make-certs.sh was planned by the SNIPS session, which wound down before doing it; nobody has it now.
